messages.content: Denver changed on me. United pushed the Wednesday flight 45 minutes later, and the conference app moved Thursday lab orientation 30 minutes earlier with badge pickup at a side registration desk. The hotel reconfirmed the queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, indoor pool, and still no hot tub. Can you sanity-check whether to keep the flight and how to route airport-hotel-badge?

Yes. If you are still not checking a bag, I would keep the shifted outbound. New arrival is 2:27 p.m., which still works. Rideshare is cleaner than airport rail for this: about 35-45 minutes curb to hotel versus rail plus transfer/walk running closer to 60-75. Use rail only if rideshare pricing is unusually high.
No checked bag. I do not want a grocery stop making the badge thing tight.

Then skip groceries before registration. Go airport to hotel, drop bags, then venue. You can buy water/snacks after badge pickup near the hotel and use the mini-fridge. Recovery note stays the same: fitness room and indoor pool confirmed; no hot tub.
What is the exact Wednesday sequence if it runs on time?

Land 2:27, request rideshare around 2:50, hotel around 3:35, check in/drop bags by 4:00, leave for the venue 4:20, side badge desk 4:35-4:45, presenter check-in immediately after. That leaves margin before the 6:30 close.
And Thursday now? Orientation is 8:00 instead of 8:30.
Leave the hotel at 7:15 Thursday. Badge is already handled, so you only need venue security and the lab-room walk. If the app shows a room change Wednesday night, keep the same departure.
Sunday checkout still okay with the 2:10 return?

Yes. I updated the file: keep the shifted United outbound, use rideshare Wednesday, no grocery stop until after badge pickup, and use straight-to-venue as the delay backup. Sunday: pack before the last morning session, back to the hotel by about 10:25, check out 10:40-10:45, and rideshare to DEN around 10:50. That protects the 2:10 p.m. DEN-TPA flight and leaves time to recheck the seat map during online check-in.

messages.content: I need a non-work weekend after Denver. We are thinking Asheville in late May, Friday to Monday, for hiking and some recovery time. Can you compare driving versus flying with a rental? I care about practical, not just cheapest, and Monday cannot wreck Tuesday prep.

For practicality, I would rank it this way: 1) Fly TPA to Greenville-Spartanburg and rent a car: best balance, roughly $260-$340 per person, more schedule choices, then 75-90 minutes to Asheville. 2) Fly into Asheville: easiest on arrival, but fares are running higher and the schedules are thinner. 3) Drive from Tampa: cheapest control, but 9.5-10.5 hours each way with stops. If Tuesday prep matters, I would not make the full drive the lead.
That is how I was leaning. What is the lodging shortlist?

Three credible choices. Downtown hotel: strong reviews, easy restaurants, easier evening walks, but no hot tub and parking adds cost. Mountain lodge: about 15 minutes outside downtown, indoor pool, hot tub, small fitness room, queen room, coffee maker, and mini-fridge; better after hiking. Cabin: quiet and trail-friendly, but Wi-Fi and room basics are unclear, cleaning fee is extra, and the cancellation window is stricter.
For this one the hot tub matters if we hike two days. I do not want to pay resort prices though.

Then the mountain lodge is the lead if the rate stays reasonable. Plain caveats: you will drive to dinner, we need to verify parking, and cancellation terms matter. Downtown wins for meals but loses the hot tub. The cabin only wins if quiet beats certainty.
How bad is the Greenville drive after landing?

GSP to the lodge is about 1 hour 15 minutes in normal traffic; add 15 minutes on a Friday evening. If you land by 4:30-5:30, get the car by 6:00, and skip complicated errands, you can be at the lodge around 7:15.
Could Asheville airport avoid enough of that to be worth it?

Only if the fare gap is small or the Asheville flight times are much cleaner. Asheville saves roughly an hour of car time, but the current options cost more and have tighter connection choices. For Monday, Greenville also has better afternoon returns, which helps protect Tuesday.
What trail base works with the lodge?

It works well for a moderate Saturday hike off the Blue Ridge Parkway or Pisgah side, then hot tub time afterward. Sunday could be a shorter hike plus spa or downtown dinner. You give up walking to restaurants, but the recovery setup is much stronger than downtown.
Let’s not book yet. My partner has to confirm Friday departure and Monday off. Put GSP plus the lodge as the practical lead, and the cabin as probably no unless the amenities come back clear.

Done. Asheville file now has Greenville-Spartanburg flight plus rental car plus mountain lodge as the practical lead. Asheville airport is the comfort upgrade only if fares drop or the schedule gets cleaner. Driving is the budget fallback, not the best choice for protecting Tuesday prep. Lodging caveats saved: lodge still needs parking and cancellation terms confirmed; downtown has easier meals but no hot tub; cabin needs Wi-Fi, coffee/fridge, and cancellation answered before I would recommend it.

messages.content: Schedule is firm: we can leave Friday after noon and Monday is free. Asheville airfare jumped, so let’s settle Greenville unless driving is obviously better.

Greenville is now the practical choice. Current pairing: Friday TPA 1:18 p.m. to GSP 4:42 p.m. via Atlanta, 58-minute layover; Monday GSP 2:25 p.m. to TPA 5:58 p.m. via Atlanta. It is $318 per person in Main Cabin. Compact rental is $186 all-in, pay at counter. Driving still saves airfare but costs 20-plus road hours and eats most of Monday.
That Monday return is fine. Are seats together with me at a window?

Yes. In Main Cabin, 12A and 12B are open outbound, and 14A and 14B are open on the return. Basic is $42 less per person, but it does not allow advance seat selection, so I would skip it if sitting together matters.
Skip basic. What did the lodge say?

The lodge confirmed the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and small fitness room. New caveats: parking is $18 per night, and free cancellation ends Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. before arrival, effectively a two-night cutoff. The rate is $229 per night before taxes.
Total versus downtown?

Lodge is about $846 for three nights with taxes and parking. Downtown is about $780 with parking, better for dinner access, and has fitness plus room fridge and coffee maker, but no hot tub. Cabin looks like $735 at first, but cleaning and prepay bring it near $870; Wi-Fi is not guaranteed and cancellation is harsher.
For once I am okay paying a little more for the hot tub and quieter base. The Greenville drive is not a deal breaker.

Then I would book the flights and compact rental, and either hold or book the lodge before that room disappears. Arrival sketch: land 4:42, rental by about 5:20, grocery stop near GSP only if the flight is on time, lodge around 6:45-7:15.
Can we do a light grocery stop only if it does not push dinner too late?

Yes. I will mark it conditional: stop for breakfast items and snacks if you are out of the rental lot by 5:30. If not, go straight to the lodge and use the mini-fridge after a quick next-morning stop.
Go ahead and book the flights and rental. For the lodge, if it can be held without charging, hold it; if not, book it with that cancellation cutoff.

Before I commit: flights are nonrefundable Main Cabin with change-credit rules; rental is pay-later; the lodge does not offer a no-card hold, charges the first night at booking, and is cancellable until Wednesday 6:00 p.m. before arrival. Does that work?
Yes. Book it. And keep me by the window, partner beside me.

Booked. Flights: Delta TPA-GSP Friday via Atlanta, 1:18 p.m.-4:42 p.m.; return Monday GSP-TPA via Atlanta, 2:25 p.m.-5:58 p.m. Seats are 12A/12B outbound and 14A/14B return. Compact rental reserved at GSP, pay at counter. Lodge booked in a queen room, confirmation ML-58219, first-night deposit charged; cancel by Wednesday 6:00 p.m. before arrival to avoid penalty.
Add the Monday timing so I do not cut it close from Asheville.

Added: leave the lodge by 10:45 Monday, return the car at GSP by 12:30, and keep the 2:25 p.m. departure. If you hike Monday morning, make it only a short local walk. Open reminders: online check-in, seat-map recheck, rental counter hours, and one dinner reservation because the lodge is not downtown.
